Well, yeah, it's definitely bleeding into everything else. My department actually had to step in recently on decisions I used to handle all by myself. Which is frustrating because I know how to run my lab. It's just... I get so caught up.

When I was younger? Um... I don't know, I guess I've always liked things to be organized. But I wouldn't say I was obsessed with rules or anything. I mean, I just liked things to make sense. 

Like when I was in middle school, I had this rock collection. I spent an entire summer cataloging them by their Mohs hardness scale and cleavage patterns. I even built this custom display case out of some scrap pine my dad had in the garage. Actually, the pine was really interesting because it had all these intricate beetle galleries carved into the sapwood. I spent hours trying to identify the specific species of bark beetle based on the gallery patterns. It's fascinating how they create these complex, branching tunnels that almost look like fractals. Did you know that some bark beetles actually cultivate fungi in those tunnels to feed their larvae? It's this incredible symbiotic relationship. I ended up reading everything I could find about forest entomology at the local library. The librarian, Mrs. Gable, she had this really peculiar way of stamping the due date cards. She would always align the stamp perfectly with the top right corner of the grid, never overlapping the lines. It was so satisfying to watch. I tried to show my brother how to do it with his library books, but he just jammed the stamp down wherever. It drove me crazy. 

But... wait, what were we talking about? Something about school?

Interfered? I don't know if I'd call it interfering. I mean, for months now, I've actually felt like the lab is finally moving at my speed. It's like I'm... electrified, you know? They just turn on the tap and expect everything to work forever without even thinking about the mineral buildup inside the pipes...\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel distressed or upset about getting sidetracked by these details, or do you feel that it’s just how you naturally work?\n\nPatient: Distressed? Function in my job? I mean, I guess... well, my department *has* had to step in lately on decisions I used to handle all by myself. I started looking up the material safety data sheets for the pigment binders they use, because I suspect they're cutting costs by using a lower-grade polymer resin. I actually emailed the manufacturer about it because it's false advertising if the cap seal isn't properly rated for the specific solvent they're using. \n\nAnyway, I spent a good chunk of the afternoon researching that, and the undergrad just left. I mean, I just liked things to make sense. \n\nLike when I was in middle school, I had this rock collection. Actually, the pine was really interesting because it had all these intricate beetle galleries carved into the sapwood. I spent hours trying to identify the specific species of bark beetle based on the gallery patterns. It's fascinating how they create these complex, branching tunnels that almost look like fractals. Did you know that some bark beetles actually cultivate fungi in those tunnels to feed their larvae? It's this incredible symbiotic relationship. I ended up reading everything I could find about forest entomology at the local library. The librarian, Mrs. Gable, she had this really peculiar way of stamping the due date cards. The pipes they used for that system are galvanized steel, which is prone to mineral scaling on the inside if the water hardness isn't managed. I got up on my desk to take the cover off the fixture, and the ballast was actually leaking this black potting compound. I realized I was standing under a potential toxic hazard, so I immediately started looking up the EPA regulations on PCB disposal under the Toxic Substances Control Act. I spent hours drafting this urgent email to the dean about the legal and environmental liabilities of pre-1979 lighting fixtures in university workspaces. I even started designing a proposal to retrofit the entire science wing with LED panels, calculating the lumen output and the energy savings over a ten-year period to offset the initial capital expenditure... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about the lighting retrofit? Oh, right, you were asking if I get upset. Yeah, I snap at the students if they tell me to slow down. What was your question again?
